data.bottom_line: Small, isolated slabs of drifted snow may exist in upper elevation terrain. Cues for identifying these are small cornices and a stiffer, thicker feel to the snow. On steep slopes, triggering these slabs could result in a harsh start and early end to your winter riding. Early-season trips are a great time to re-aquaint yourself with your avalanche safety systems - pre-trip plans, beacon and equipment checks, mid-day conditions check-ins, and one-at-a-time riding. Practice these now, so they'll be quicker, smoother, and less likely to fail when the great riding arrives.
